name: Odometry
description: PicoB turns the IMU and the wheel counts into the pose, speeds and tilt, and reports them to PicoA 50 times a second; PicoA keeps them as a history to place each ToF frame.

steps.name: robot frame
steps.what: the sensor's axes into the robot's (the mounting)

steps.name: heading
steps.what: gyro z, less its bias, into the heading

steps.name: wheels
steps.what: the wheel counts (flow wheel-counts) into distance, speed and position

steps.name: tilt
steps.what: acceleration and gyro into pitch and roll (filter, 0.5 s)

steps.name: report
steps.what: the fields PicoA needs, plus the motors' state and why they stopped

steps.name: PicoA's clock
steps.what: learns PicoB's clock from each report's time, so its times can be read on PicoA's

steps.name: history
steps.what: each report into the pose history (~1.3 s): roll and the motors' state dropped

steps.name: interpolate
steps.what: the history into the pose at the frame's middle (the private at(), not pose_at())

name: Wheel counts
description: The four encoder counts, read by odometry each IMU sample and joined into the pose.

name: Tilt stop
description: PicoB switches the motors off when pitch or roll passes 15°; only the two angles are read out of odometry.

name: IMU to the PC
description: The IMU's raw counts, averaged 4 to 1 on PicoB, carried through PicoA in batches of 10 during a move and stored on the PC as training data.

steps.name: average 4
steps.what: 4 samples in a row averaged into one record, stamped with their middle time

steps.name: PicoA's clock
steps.what: the record's time from PicoB's clock to PicoA's

steps.name: batch
steps.what: up to 10 records in a row into a batch with the move's number; a gap starts a new batch

steps.name: 64-bit time
steps.what: the first record's time into µs since power-up (never wraps); the others by the period

steps.name: encode
steps.what: into the imu batch message: 15 B header, 12 B a record (the records' own times dropped)

steps.name: decode
steps.what: the bytes into records, each with its own time again

steps.name: seconds
steps.what: numbered as the boot's next message; times in seconds

name: ToF frame to the PC
description: Each ToF frame, placed where the robot was while it measured, packed small and sent to the PC during a move; the PC stores it.

steps.name: pose
steps.what: the pose at the frame's middle, the turn during it, still or not (flow odometry)

steps.name: 64-bit time
steps.what: the frame's time into µs since power-up (never wraps), for the message

steps.name: encode
steps.what: the move's number and the 64-bit time (12 B), then the frame packed for the map use (277 B: 8-bit distances)
steps.code: uint32_t wire_encode_tof(tof_use_t use, uint32_t move, uint64_t t_us, const posed_frame_t *f, uint8_t *out) {

steps.name: decode
steps.what: the move's number and time read; the rest handed to unpackTof

steps.name: unpack
steps.what: the packed frame into zones and a pose, the robot's units

steps.name: seconds
steps.what: numbered as the boot's next message; time in seconds

name: ToF frame to the robot's map
description: Each posed frame, packed and unpacked as the PC gets it, into the robot's 6 × 6 m window. Ground-layer ray passes beyond 50 cm are ignored, so distant floor reflections do not mark holes.

steps.name: pack
steps.what: into the map use's format (compact: 8-bit distances)

steps.name: unpack
steps.what: back into a frame: the same data the PC gets

name: ToF frame to watch
description: Each posed frame, packed and unpacked for the watch use, into watch, which looks for movement.

steps.name: pack
steps.what: into the watch use's format (today the same compact format)

steps.name: unpack
steps.what: back into a frame

name: Command
description: A steering command from the viewer: through the server's queue to the robot, where it starts a move.

steps.what: "steer d50" into checked commands (one per letter)
steps.code: const parsed: Parsed = name === "steer" || name === "check" ? parseSteer(arg)

steps.name: auto snap
steps.what: a snap after each move, when auto_snap is on (robot config auto_snap)

steps.name: robot text
steps.what: into the robot's words ("drive 50") with the next command number

steps.name: encode
steps.what: into the command message: number and text (up to 46 characters)

steps.name: decode

steps.name: parse on the robot
steps.what: the text into an action and its numbers (cm into m)

name: Answer
description: How a move ended, from the robot back to the server, which answers the command and puts the answer in everyone's log.

steps.name: answer
steps.what: the move's record and the pose now (body_odometry) into the command's answer

steps.name: encode

steps.name: decode

steps.name: done record

steps.name: outcome

name: Drive startup checked against the map
description: Before starting a drive, the robot checks its 6 × 6 m map for obstacles and drops across the requested distance, and on a forward drive for unidentified floor within 25 cm ahead, stopping 15 cm short. This flow shows startup refusal, not the repeated checks while moving.

steps.name: room
steps.what: less the robot's front or rear and the 15 cm stop margin
steps.code: return gap(x_m, y_m, yaw_rad, direction, look_m, &g) ? g - STOP_BEFORE_M : look_m;

steps.name: drive limit
steps.what: into how far the drive may go, and whether an obstacle stops it short

name: PC cell map
description: The PC builds a boot's whole-house cell map (6 × 6 m window and 2 × 2 m tiles) from the boot's stored ToF frames by running the robot's own C map code in a helper process.

steps.code: const frames = await this.store.framesBetween(boot, b.fedUpTo, lastFrame);

steps.name: pack for helper
steps.what: each stored frame into its 277 B compact bytes for the C helper
steps.code: add(frame: PosedFrame): Promise<Buffer> { return this.ask("F", packTof("compact", frame)); }

steps.name: build map
steps.what: the helper runs cell_map_add and house_map (2 × 2 m tiles), and returns the window, columns and tiles
steps.code: const view = kept ?? await this.upTo(boot, s.lastFrame, m => m.view());

name: Robot's map on demand
description: When asked (robot map --robot), the robot sends its 6 × 6 m window in 9 bulk messages. Requests run one at a time. The PC waits for both the window and the command answer's live pose: the control answer may arrive before the bulk parts. The C helper classifies the columns; this does not use a snapshot or the PC's stored tiles.

steps.name: encode part
steps.what: 1,200 cell bytes (1/9 of the window) and the window's origin into one map part message
steps.code: uint32_t len = wire_encode_map_part(part, (int16_t)ox, (int16_t)oy, cells + part * WIRE_MAP_PART_CELLS, message);

steps.name: decode part
steps.what: the bytes into one of the 9 map parts

steps.name: join 9 parts
steps.what: the 9 parts in order into the 10,800 B window and its origin
steps.code: this.emit("mapWindow", { originX: mapOriginCx, originY: mapOriginCy, cellsX: 60, cellsY: 60, cells: Buffer.concat(mapParts) });

steps.name: live pose
steps.what: the map command's control answer (flow map-answer) supplies the live pose; return only when both answer and window have arrived
steps.code: else if (d && w) finish({ window: w, pose: d.pose });
return this.runner.askMap ? this.runner.askMap() : Promise.resolve({ error: "robot not connected" });

steps.name: columns
steps.what: the C helper's cell_map_column_of turns the 3 layers into 60 × 60 columns and confidence (--png)
steps.code: const b = await this.ask("K", cells), colBytes = GRID * GRID;

name: Map command's answer
description: The map command's answer uses the same control-message path as other answers. Its command number selects the waiting request; its result and live pose join the bulk window in robot-map.
